newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mercedes-Benz sees Mexico sales doubling in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes-Benz sees Mexico sales doubling in 1997.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz could double its sales in Mexico to 16,000 bus and truck units this year over 1996, but it won't reach its 1994 mark on sales until 2000, a company official said.

"Personally, I think returning to the figures of 1994 will happen in 2000," Federico Korte, president of Mercedes-Benz de Mexico, told Reuters in an interview Wednesday at the inauguration of the company's National Parts Distribution Center (CDP) in this north-central Mexican state.
"We are really happy because we see that the economy is recovering in giant steps ... particularly in our segment, we see that our total market will double compared to last year," Korte said.
In 1994, Mercedes-Benz sold about 33,000 commercial vehicles, but its sales tumbled to 5,000 in 1995, Korte said.
Sales recovered to about 8,000 units last year.
"This year we estimate we are going to double to 16,000 units, which is a good recovery," Korte said.

Automobile sales in Mexico plummeted in 1995 in the economic crisis sparked by the sudden peso devaluation in December 1994, with overall sales falling from nearly 600,000 in 1994 to about 226,000 in 1995, according to the Mexican Association of the Automobile Industry.

Korte said Mercedes-Benz located its parts distribution center here with an eye toward the United States. San Luis Potos is on the so-called "Nafta Highway," a trade route named after the North American Free Trade Agreement.
"We believe Nafta is a fundamental topic and that we are going to see more and more trucks passing along this route, and for that reason it's important to be here," Korte said.
In addition, San Luis Potos is within a 300-mile (500-km) roundtrip to 80 percent of the company's distributors, he said.
The new $15.5 million plant is expected to generate sales of 400 million pesos (about $50 million) a year in Mexico, Korte said.
"For 1997, parts sales volumes will be about $32 million, which is about 10 percent of the total invoicing for Mercedes-Benz (de Mxico)," Korte said later in a news conference.
Mexican auto parts sales totaled $28 million in 1996, he said.
